ranked_evidence.title: Trump news at a glance: president returns to old playbook of undermining US election integrity - The Guardian
ranked_evidence.snippet: # Trump news at a glance: president returns to old playbook of undermining US election integrity. Experts worry Trump’s administration – now stocked with loyalists and election deniers – may not stand up to attempts to sabotage upcoming elections – key US politics stories from Tuesday 9 June at a glance. Donald Trump is “inventing fraud” in California’s primary elections, and likely to ramp up unfounded allegations when more races go against him, pro-democracy experts have warned. While the US president has used this playbook for years – from his loss at the Emmys as a reality TV star to his defeat in the 2020 presidential election – election integrity campaigners fear this time could be different. “California’s election is not the problem here,” said Omar Noureldin, senior vice-president of policy and litigation at Common Cause, a pro-democracy watchdog group. “The problem is that we have a president in the Oval Office who continues to lie and sow doubt over elections instead of facing accountability from voters.”.

BJP's recent gains, especially in West Bengal, have expanded its dominance across North, West, Central, East, and Northeast India, making it a pan-India force. The latest round of assembly election results 2026, especially the party’s surge in West Bengal, has sharpened a trend that has been building for over a decade: the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) is now the dominant political force across most regions of India, while the Congress finds itself increasingly confined to the South. With leads in Bengal adding to its tally, the BJP’s footprint now spans North, West, Central, East and the Northeast, making this one of the most geographically expansive phases in the party’s history.
